landmarks.name: Riga Old Town
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site known for its medieval architecture and vibrant cultural scene.

wiki.extract: Riga, officially Riga State City, is the capital, primate, and largest city of Latvia and the second largest in the Baltics. Home to 588,911 inhabitants, the city accounts for a third of Latvia's total population. The population of Riga metropolitan area, which stretches beyond the city limits, is estimated at 847,162. The city lies on the Gulf of Riga at the mouth of the Daugava river where it meets the Baltic Sea. Riga's territory covers 307.17 km2 (118.60 sq mi) and lies 1–10 m (3–33 ft) above sea level on a flat and sandy plain.

landmarks.name: Gauja National Park
landmarks.writeup: The largest national park in Latvia, famous for its natural beauty, hiking trails, and historic castles.

wiki.extract: Gauja National Park in Vidzeme is the largest national park in Latvia, with an area of 917.86 km2 running from north-east of Sigulda to south-west of Cēsis along the valley of the Gauja River, from which the park takes its name.

landmarks.name: Rundnle Palace
landmarks.writeup: An 18th-century Baroque palace often referred to as the 'Versailles of Latvia'.

cultural_events.name: Latvian Song and Dance Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A massive cultural event held every five years celebrating Latvian folk music and dance.

wiki.extract: The Latvian Song and Dance Festival is one of the largest amateur choral and dancing events in the world, and an important event in Latvian culture and social life.

cultural_events.name: Jnni (Midsummer Festival)
cultural_events.writeup: A traditional celebration marking the summer solstice with singing, dancing, and bonfires.

food_writeup: Latvian cuisine features hearty dishes with rye bread, potatoes, pork, and dairy products, emphasizing seasonal and locally sourced ingredients.
brief_history: Latvia has a history of foreign rule by Germans, Swedes, Poles, and Russians before gaining independence in 1918. It was occupied by the Soviet Union during WWII and regained independence in 1991.

important_people.name: Rainis
important_people.description: Poet and playwright, a key figure in Latvian literature.

important_people.name: Vaira Vnne-Freiberga
important_people.description: Former President and influential political leader.

current_conflicts: Latvia is not involved in any active internal or external conflicts but remains vigilant due to regional security concerns related to Russia.
